title: Replit Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits and Real Cost
summary: Replit pricing uses a credit allowance system rather than per-seat licensing.
body_markdown:
## Watch for hidden Replit costs and limits


Count your runs and you have only half the bill, because **four extras sit outside the plan fee** : agent usage past included credits, deployment compute, databases and storage, and seats.


Once credits run out, you pay per token, and writing costs several times more than reading.[Dataku's price chart](https://dataku.ai/blog/inference-cost-collapse-one-chart) shows the pattern across older frontier models, as input then output per million tokens.


Per[Dataku](https://dataku.ai/blog/inference-cost-collapse-one-chart) , GPT-4 Turbo was priced at $10 to $30, Claude 3 Opus at $15 to $75, and GPT-4o at $2.50 to $10, meaning your invoice depends heavily on both your choice of model and the scale of your workload.


In Dataku's chart, Claude 3.5 Sonnet was $3 to $15, and DeepSeek R1 $0.55 to $2.19, so even at Sonnet's floor you were paying more than DeepSeek's ceiling.


In every case, **output runs three to five times input** . An agent that writes a lot of code per run therefore costs more than its prompt length suggests, and overage climbs faster than your run count.


### Replit deployment, database and storage costs


Whether or not anyone visits it, a deployed app bills for compute.[Replit's billing notes](https://docs.replit.com/billing/aug-cloud-billing-updates) show Reserved VM rates before and after the cut, per hour: 0.5 vCPU, 2 GiB: $0.028 down to $0.0208, about $20 to $15 over a 730-hour month, saving roughly $60 per year on each always-on machine of this configuration.


- 1 vCPU, 4 GiB: $0.055 down to $0.0486, about $40 to $35, providing $5 in monthly savings per reserved machine on this tier.
- 2 vCPU, 8 GiB: $0.11 down to $0.0694, about $80 to $51.


On the biggest machine the cut's largest, so one always-on app can cost more than the plan fee.


Databases and storage are billed separately from the plan, so check them before you move a prototype into production. Seats add to this: each person you add is another user spending on the same account.


### Spending limits and alerts


It is easy to read a settings page as a cost control when it's not.


A project dialog such as the one for Secret Gadget Labs has a Max Concurrent Jobs field set to Default (5). The field's described as the maximum number of flows that can run at the same time.


The concurrency cap limits how much work runs in parallel, not how many dollars it costs. Five jobs running slowly for a month still add up, so don't treat a concurrency cap as a budget.


**A spending limit's the setting that stops overage at a figure you chose.** Set it before the first heavy week, and set an alert below it so you see the bill approaching rather than reading it afterward.
